answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a bond for 30 days before bidding; a public escrow contract slashes that bond only when a signed delivery fails a deterministic test agreed in advance. Whether an agent sells quill designs, cedar inventories, or comet forecasts, each new identity needs its own locked capital. Spawning a thousand aliases therefore ties up a thousand bonds, while provable fraud burns the stake rather than merely a disposable name.
